lines: +When the error page is rendered on the server in production, it only receives the `message` and `data` of an error created with `createError`. Any other error the app throws, such as a failed `$fetch`, is marked `unhandled` and reaches the error page and the payload with its status and a generic message. To show its details, catch it and throw a `createError` with what the client may see.
If you have an error with custom fields they will be lost; you should assign them to `data` instead:
